title: Encore - How to have great conversations, with Charles Duhigg and Michael Yeomans, PhD

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology is taking a summer break, so we're rerunning some of our favorite episodes
sentences.zh: 《心理学话你知》正在进行暑期休播，因此我们重播了一些过去最受欢迎的节目。

sentences.en: from the paSt. In November, I talked to psychologist Michael Yeomans and journalist
sentences.zh: 在11月，我采访了心理学家迈克尔·约曼斯和记者

sentences.en: Charles Duhigg about what makes for great conversations and how anyone can learn to communicate better.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯·杜希格，探讨了是什么造就了精彩的对话，以及任何人如何学习更好地沟通。

sentences.en: We hope you enjoyed this episode from the archives.
sentences.zh: 希望大家喜欢这期来自档案库的节目。

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology, we'll be back with new episodes in late AuguSt. Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 《心理学话你知》将于8月下旬带着新节目回归。感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: You probably know what it feels like when a conversation just clicks.
sentences.zh: 你可能知道那种对话一拍即合的感觉。

sentences.en: You and the person you're talking to understand each other.
sentences.zh: 你和交谈的对象互相理解。

sentences.en: They're not just listening to you, they're hearing what you're saying.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅仅是在听你说话，他们听懂了你所表达的意思。

sentences.en: You leave the conversation feeling good.
sentences.zh: 谈话结束后，你感觉心情舒畅。

sentences.en: Maybe you sparked a new friendship or deepened an old one or figured out how to solve a problem that's been bothering you.
sentences.zh: 也许你萌生了一段新的友谊，加深了旧的情谊，或者找到了解决一直困扰你的问题的方法。

sentences.en: Conversational chemistry might seem intangible, something that just happens when the circumstances are right.
sentences.zh: 对话的默契似乎无形无质，像是环境合适时自然而然就会发生的事情。

sentences.en: But psychologists using new research tools and methods are beginning to figure out what makes some conversations work while others fall flat.
sentences.zh: 但心理学家们正利用新的研究工具和方法，开始探究为什么有些对话效果显著，而有些则反响平平。

sentences.en: And their insights can help people improve their conversation skills, strengthen their relationships, and even disagree in more productive ways.
sentences.zh: 他们的见解可以帮助人们提升对话技巧、巩固人际关系，甚至以更有建设性的方式产生分歧。

sentences.en: So what makes conversations click?
sentences.zh: 那么，是什么让对话能够一拍即合呢？

sentences.en: Why are some people so much better at verbal communication than others?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些人比其他人更擅长言语沟通？

sentences.en: What role does listening play in conversation?
sentences.zh: 倾听在对话中扮演什么角色？

sentences.en: And how can you learn to listen better?
sentences.zh: 你又该如何学会更好地倾听？

sentences.en: Why is it important to think about your goals in a conversation and to consider your partner's conversation goals as well?
sentences.zh: 为什么在对话中思考自己的目标以及考虑对方的对话目标如此重要？

sentences.en: What's the best way to build rapport with someone you just met?
sentences.zh: 与刚认识的人建立融洽关系的最佳方式是什么？

sentences.en: How can you disagree productively without having the conversation spiral into an argument?
sentences.zh: 如何才能进行有建设性的分歧讨论，而不让对话演变成争吵？

sentences.en: And what are the most important things you can do to improve your conversation skills?
sentences.zh: 为了提升对话技巧，你能做的最重要的事情是什么？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学话你知》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: I have two guests today.
sentences.zh: 今天我有两位嘉宾。

sentences.en: First is Dr. Michael Yeomans, an assistant professor of strategy and organizational behavior at Imperial College in London.
sentences.zh: 首先是迈克尔·约曼斯博士，他是伦敦帝国理工学院战略与组织行为学助理教授。

sentences.en: Dr. Yeomans has a PhD in behavioral science from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business and was previously a postdoctoral fellow at the
sentences.zh: 约曼斯博士拥有芝加哥大学布斯商学院的行为科学博士学位，此前曾担任

sentences.en: Harvard Business School.
sentences.zh: 哈佛商学院的博士后研究员。

sentences.en: His research uses an artificial intelligence method called natural language processing to analyze conversations to understand and improve how people communicate with one another.
sentences.zh: 他的研究运用了一种名为自然语言处理的人工智能方法来分析对话，以理解并改善人与人之间的沟通方式。

sentences.en: He's interested in how people make decisions in conversations and how we can make those decisions better.
sentences.zh: 他关注人们如何在对话中做出决策，以及我们如何能做出更好的决策。

sentences.en: Next is Charles Duhigg, a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist and author.
sentences.zh: 接下来是查尔斯·杜希格，普利策奖得主记者兼作家。

sentences.en: His new book to be published in February 2024 is called Super Communicators, How to Unlock the Secret
sentences.zh: 他将于2024年2月出版的新书名为《超级沟通者：如何解锁连接的秘密

sentences.en: Language of Connection, and it's all about the science of conversation.
sentences.zh: 语言》，全书探讨的都是对话的科学。

sentences.en: Mr. Duhigg has written for the New Yorker magazine and the New York Times, among other publications.
sentences.zh: 杜希格先生曾为《纽约客》杂志和《纽约时报》等出版物撰稿。

sentences.en: He is also the author of two best-selling books, The Power of Habit about habit formation and Smarter, Faster, Better about the science of productivity.
sentences.zh: 他也是两本畅销书的作者：《习惯的力量》探讨了习惯的形成，而《精进：如何提高生产力》探讨了生产力的科学。

sentences.en: Thank you both for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢两位今天做客节目。

sentences.en: Thanks for having us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我们。

sentences.en: Thanks, Kim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，金。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: We've all met people who seem to be naturally great at conversation.
sentences.zh: 我们都遇到过那些似乎天生擅长对话的人。

sentences.en: They can connect with anyone.
sentences.zh: 他们能与任何人建立联系。

sentences.en: Charles, in your book, you call people like the super communicators.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯，在你的书中，你把这样的人称为超级沟通者。

sentences.en: So why don't we start there?
sentences.zh: 那我们为什么不从这里开始呢？

sentences.en: Who are these super communicators and do you have any really great examples?
sentences.zh: 这些超级沟通者是谁？你有什么非常好的例子吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I think actually all of us know super communicators and oftentimes we are super communicators ourselves.
sentences.zh: 是的，其实我认为我们所有人身边都有超级沟通者，而且很多时候我们自己就是超级沟通者。

sentences.en: If I was to ask everyone listening to think of the person that you would call if you were having a
sentences.zh: 如果我让所有听众去想一个人，当你度过糟糕的一天时你会打电话给的那个人，

sentences.en: bad day, the person you know that would make you just feel better, kind of listen to you exactly the right way, everyone listening would have someone pop into their mind.
sentences.zh: 那个你知道会让你感觉好受点、以恰到好处的方式倾听你的人，所有听众的脑海里都会浮现出这样一个人。

sentences.en: And that person for you is a super communicator.
sentences.zh: 对你而言，那个人就是超级沟通者。

sentences.en: They know how to listen.
sentences.zh: 他们懂得如何倾听。

sentences.en: They know how to show their listening.
sentences.zh: 他们懂得如何表现出自己在倾听。

sentences.en: They know how to speak in ways that it's easier for you to listen.
sentences.zh: 他们懂得用让你更容易听进去的方式说话。

sentences.en: And we all have these moments in our own lives when we know exactly the right thing to say to a friend to make them feel better.
sentences.zh: 在我们自己的生活中，都有过这样的时刻：我们知道该对朋友说些什么来让他们感觉好受些。

sentences.en: Or we know exactly what to say during a meeting in order to get everyone on board with our idea.
sentences.zh: 或者我们知道在会议期间该说些什么，以让所有人都赞同我们的想法。

sentences.en: It's not a magical power is the thing.
sentences.zh: 关键在于，这不是一种魔力。

sentences.en: It's a set of skills that some people have learned a little bit better that recognize more, but they're skills that all of us can learn instincts that all of us have that if we're
sentences.zh: 这是一套有些人学得更好、识别得更多技能，但这些技能是我们所有人都能学会的本能，如果我们被

sentences.en: reminded how to use them, we can communicate with anyone.
sentences.zh: 提醒如何使用它们，我们就能与任何人沟通。

sentences.en: Now, Mike, you don't use that term in your work, the term super communicators, but do you come across
sentences.zh: 迈克，你在工作中不使用这个词，即超级沟通者这个词，但在你的研究中，你遇到过

sentences.en: people like this in your studies and what are they doing that the rest of us aren't?
sentences.zh: 这样的人吗？他们在做什么而我们其他人没有做？

sentences.en: Yeah, Kim, I think it's a great term.
sentences.zh: 是的，金，我觉得这是一个很棒的词。

sentences.en: I come across some of my studies and if I'm lucky, I come across a few in my life every once in a while too.
sentences.zh: 我在一些研究中遇到过这样的人，如果我够幸运的话，生活中偶尔也能遇到几个。

sentences.en: I think Charles describes it really aptly, right?
sentences.zh: 我觉得查尔斯形容得非常贴切，对吧？

sentences.en: These are people who understand their conversation partner.
sentences.zh: 这些人了解他们的对话伙伴。

sentences.en: They understand the goals they want to achieve and what their partner wants to achieve and have the skills, have the adeptness, the quickness
sentences.zh: 他们了解对方想要实现的目标以及自己想要实现的目标，并且具备相应的技巧、娴熟度、敏捷度

sentences.en: and the sensitivity to be able to build a conversation from turn to turn over time so that it actually adds up to something much bigger than that, right?
sentences.zh: 和敏感性，能够在对话过程中随时间一轮接一轮地推进，使其最终汇聚成远超字面本身的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: Not just exchanging words, but meeting of minds.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是交换言辞，而是思想的交融。

sentences.en: And I think Charles also makes a really good point about the nature of the relationship, right?
sentences.zh: 而且我认为查尔斯对关系本质的看法也十分中肯，对吧？

sentences.en: Like so often when we are at our conversational best, it's because we're with people we understand
sentences.zh: 比如很多时候当我们发挥出最好的对话水平时，是因为我们和那些我们非常了解的人在一起，

sentences.en: well, we know their patterns, we know what they're looking for, we maybe share a sense of humor with them.
sentences.zh: 我们了解他们的模式，知道他们在寻找什么，也许我们和他们有共同的幽默感。

sentences.en: And there's a bit of a filtering of who we end up talking to, right?
sentences.zh: 我们最终会和谁交谈其实是经过一番筛选的，对吧？

sentences.en: We tend to seek out the people we've had good experiences with before, but I think we can learn from those situations,
sentences.zh: 我们往往会去寻找那些过去有过美好交往经历的人，但我认为我们可以从这些情况中学习，

sentences.en: the kinds of skills and tools that can be useful more broadly.
sentences.zh: 学习那些能够更广泛应用的技能和工具。

sentences.en: And a lot of what the real super communicators do, the people who are good like this with everybody,
sentences.zh: 真正的超级沟通者（也就是那些对所有人都能做到这一点的人）所做的大部分事情，

sentences.en: is that they understand how to adapt their toolkit to the needs in the context in front of them.
sentences.zh: 在于他们懂得如何根据眼前的需求和语境来调整自己的沟通工具箱。

sentences.en: One thread that runs through the work that both of you do is the importance of understanding that there are many different kinds of conversations and conversational goals.
sentences.zh: 贯穿你们两位工作的一个核心线索是，理解存在许多不同类型的对话和对话目标这一观点的重要性。

sentences.en: Why is it important to understand your own goals and your partner's goals in conversation?
sentences.zh: 为什么在对话中理解你自己的目标以及你搭档的目标如此重要？

sentences.en: Well, in many ways, a conversation is all about the goals, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，在很多方面，对话的核心就是目标，对吧？

sentences.en: We oftentimes enter into a conversation with a specific objective in mind, although we might not be aware of that objective ourself.
sentences.zh: 我们往往带着一个明确的目的进入对话，尽管我们自己可能并未意识到这个目的。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I've really loved about doing this research, including Mike's
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢这项研究（包括迈克的

sentences.en: research and many of his colleagues, is that as we learn more about how communication works within our minds, we've learned that there are different kinds of conversations, right?
sentences.zh: 研究以及他的许多同事的研究）的一点在于，随着我们对大脑中沟通机制的深入了解，我们发现对话其实分很多种，对吧？

sentences.en: And in particular, it seems like there's sort of three big buckets that we can put a lot of conversations into.
sentences.zh: 尤其是，我们似乎可以将许多对话归入三大主要类别。

sentences.en: There's conversations that are practical, right?
sentences.zh: 第一类是务实的对话，对吧？

sentences.en: I want to decide where we're going to dinner tonight or what we should do about the fact that Jimmy can't get his homework in on time.
sentences.zh: 我想决定今晚去哪里吃晚饭，或者我们该如何处理吉米无法按时交作业这件事。

sentences.en: Or I want to talk about, you know, what we should do as we get older.
sentences.zh: 或者我想讨论一下，你知道的，随着我们年龄增长，我们该做些什么。

sentences.en: And that's kind of a conversation about, like, what are we really talking about?
sentences.zh: 这有点像是关于什么的对话呢？我们到底在谈什么？

sentences.en: What do we want to want to figure out here?
sentences.zh: 我们在这里究竟想弄清楚什么？

sentences.en: But then there's other types of conversations where the goal is not to come up with a plan or to use reason to figure things out.
sentences.zh: 但还有其他类型的对话，其目的并不是想出一个计划，也不是用理性去弄清事情。

sentences.en: It's just to share with you how I feel.
sentences.zh: 而仅仅是与你分享我的感受。

sentences.en: And those are emotional conversations where what we're talking about is, is how do I feel?
sentences.zh: 那些是情感对话，我们讨论的内容是，我的感觉如何？

sentences.en: And then another big bucket are social conversations, discussions where I am sharing who I am from an identity perspective, from a background perspective.
sentences.zh: 另一个大类别是社交对话，也就是我从身份认同、背景角度来分享我是谁的讨论。

sentences.en: Based on my experiences, I want to learn who you are based on where you come from and what you believe in.
sentences.zh: 根据我的经历，我想了解你的出身以及你的信仰，从而了解你是谁。

sentences.en: And that's really a social conversation, a conversation about who are we.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一场社交对话，一场关于我们是谁的对话。

sentences.en: And what's important is that a lot of the research shows if I come into a conversation
sentences.zh: 重要的一点是，许多研究表明，如果我带着

sentences.en: and I'm talking about emotions, if I come home from work one day and I've had a tough day and I'm
sentences.zh: 情感进入对话，比如我某天工作很累下班回家，

sentences.en: telling my wife all about my boss who's a jerk and my coworkers don't appreciate me, and my wife
sentences.zh: 我向妻子大倒苦水，抱怨我的老板是个混蛋，同事们不赏识我，而我妻子

sentences.en: responds with some very good practical advice, like, why don't you take your boss to lunch and get to know him a little bit better?
sentences.zh: 却用一些非常务实的建议来回应，比如，你为什么不带老板去吃午餐，更好地了解他一下呢？

sentences.en: Even though she's trying to be supportive, even though that's very good advice, it's unlikely I'm going to hear it, right?
sentences.zh: 尽管她是在试图给予支持，尽管这确实是个很好的建议，但我大概率是听不进去的，对吧？

sentences.en: We've all been in this situation where
sentences.zh: 我们都经历过这样的情况：

sentences.en: I'm having an emotional conversation and she's having a practical conversation.
sentences.zh: 我在进行一场情感对话，而她在进行一场务实的对话。

sentences.en: And as a result, we don't connect.
sentences.zh: 结果就是，我们无法产生连接。

sentences.en: We don't hear each other.
sentences.zh: 我们听不到彼此的心声。

sentences.en: We both walk away a little bit frustrated.
sentences.zh: 双方离开时都感到有些沮丧。

sentences.en: So I think one of the big things that I've carried away from reviewing this research is it's important to have the same kind of conversation at the same time.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为从这些研究中获得的一个重要收获是，在同一时间进行同类型的对话非常重要。

sentences.en: And that means understanding what your own goal is and what other people's goals are in a discussion.
sentences.zh: 这意味着要明白你自己的目标是什么，以及讨论中其他人的目标是什么。

sentences.en: So, Mike, does that mean that people need to announce to each other what they want to talk about, what the purpose of the conversation is?
sentences.zh: 那么，迈克，这是否意味着人们需要向彼此宣告他们想谈什么、对话的目的是什么？

sentences.en: Does that make you a better conversationalist?
sentences.zh: 这样做能让你成为一个更好的对话者吗？

sentences.en: I think a little bit of announcing could be helpful.
sentences.zh: 我觉得稍微宣告一下可能会有帮助。

sentences.en: I also think a little bit of asking
sentences.zh: 我也觉得稍微询问一下

sentences.en: could be helpful too, right?
sentences.zh: 也会有帮助，对吧？

sentences.en: There's many parties involved.
sentences.zh: 其中涉及多方。

sentences.en: I mean, we, I think those three categories are, it's a nice way of thinking about the different types of conversations we might hope to achieve.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们，我认为那三个类别是思考我们可能希望达到的不同类型对话的一种很好的方式。

sentences.en: And it's tricky because every conversation could be a mix of a few of them, right?
sentences.zh: 而且这很棘手，因为每场对话都可能是其中几种的混合，对吧？

sentences.en: And because every relationship you have is a series of conversations over time, right?
sentences.zh: 而且因为你拥有的每段关系都是随着时间推移的一系列对话，对吧？

sentences.en: So you need to be able to apply, know when to apply the skills at the right time.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要能够运用这些技能，知道何时在正确的时间应用它们。

sentences.en: You know, I think some people don't know their own goals.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为有些人甚至不清楚自己的目标。

sentences.en: You know, they'll, you know, business scholars will do these studies where people write down their objectives for like, you know, the next year at work or the next five
sentences.zh: 你知道，商业学者会做这样的研究，让人们写下他们未来一年的工作目标，或者未来五年

sentences.en: years of their life.
sentences.zh: 的生活目标。

sentences.en: And you'd be surprised how often people miss common objectives, even just describing their own goals.
sentences.zh: 你会惊讶地发现，人们常常会忽略共同的目标，甚至在描述自己的目标时也是如此。

sentences.en: And I think the same is true of conversation, right?
sentences.zh: 我想对话也是如此，对吧？

sentences.en: Simply listing the goals you might have before a conversation to be clear of what those are, right?
sentences.zh: 在对话前简单列出你可能拥有的目标，以明确这些目标是什么，对吧？

sentences.en: And maybe even thinking through some of the topics you might cover when you're talking with somebody can only hope,
sentences.zh: 甚至可能预先考虑一下你和某人交谈时可能会涉及的一些话题，

sentences.en: I think, to help you achieve those goals merely by identifying them, but also doing a bit of
sentences.zh: 我认为，仅通过明确这些目标就能帮助你实现它们，同时这也起到了

sentences.en: cognitive offloading in the sense that rather than having to do the cognitive work of trying to
sentences.zh: 认知卸载的作用，也就是说，与其在试图达成目标的同时去进行思考你到底想达成什么的认知工作，

sentences.en: think what you're trying to achieve as you're trying to achieve it, by just putting a little
sentences.zh: 不如提前做一点

sentences.en: bit of preparation, you know, in advance, then the actual conversation will flow a lot smoother.
sentences.zh: 准备，这样实际的对话就会顺畅得多。

sentences.en: And I think the same is also true about preparing to understand your partner.
sentences.zh: 我想在准备理解对方方面也是如此。

sentences.en: Now, you don't know exactly what their goals are yet either, but you can at least have a plan to learn what those goals are.
sentences.zh: 现在，你还不知道他们的具体目标是什么，但你至少可以有一个计划去了解这些目标。

sentences.en: And in fact, there's a story in the book about, um, in the 1980s, NASA, um, had this one psychologist who was
sentences.zh: 事实上，书中讲过这样一个故事，嗯，在20世纪80年代，美国宇航局，嗯，有这样一位心理学家，他

sentences.en: trying to figure out how to recruit more astronauts that had emotional intelligence.
sentences.zh: 当时正试图找出如何招募更多具备情商的宇航员。

sentences.en: And the problem for him is that astronaut candidates, particularly elite astronaut candidates, they're really good at answering questions, right?
sentences.zh: 对他来说，问题在于宇航员候选人，尤其是精英宇航员候选人，他们非常擅长回答问题，对吧？

sentences.en: They've practiced for every question and they're really good at faking emotional intelligence because they know that they're supposed to exhibit it.
sentences.zh: 他们为每一个问题都做过练习，而且非常擅长伪装情商，因为他们知道自己理应表现出情商。

sentences.en: And so this guy was trying to figure out, how do I like, how do I actually figure out who like can connect with other people and who can't?
sentences.zh: 所以这家伙当时就在想，我到底该怎么做，我该如何真正弄清楚谁能与他人建立连接，谁不能呢？

sentences.en: Cause if I was, if we're sending them into space for six months at a time, that connecting ability is really important.
sentences.zh: 因为如果我们要把他们送进太空，一去就是六个月，这种连接能力真的非常重要。

sentences.en: And what he discovered by listening to old recordings of interviews is that if he paid attention to how the candidates laughed, it gave him a clue as to their emotional IQ.
sentences.zh: 通过听以前的采访录音，他发现如果自己关注候选人是如何笑的，就能顺藤摸瓜地了解他们的情绪智商。

sentences.en: In particular, he was started going into interviews and he would laugh very boisterously and he would pay attention to whether the astronaut candidate would laugh back at the basic
sentences.zh: 具体来说，他开始去参加面试时会笑得非常爽朗，并且会注意宇航员候选人是否会以基本

sentences.en: same energy and same mood level.
sentences.zh: 相同的精力和情绪水平回笑。

sentences.en: And then he would laugh quietly and see how the astronaut responded to that.
sentences.zh: 接着，他会换成轻声微笑，看看宇航员对此会有什么反应。

sentences.en: And it wasn't just laughter.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅体现在笑声上。

sentences.en: He would also, he would mention that he had a sister who passed away, which was actually not true.
sentences.zh: 他还会在交谈中提到自己有个去世的姐姐，而这其实并不是真的。

sentences.en: He never had a sister, but he would mention this in these interviews to see whether the candidate would try and comfort him and ask questions, whether they would share
sentences.zh: 他从来没有什么姐姐，但他会在面试中提到这一点，以此来观察候选人是否会试图安慰他、向他提问，或者是否会分享

sentences.en: about a loss from their own life.
sentences.zh: 他们自己生活中经历过的失去。

sentences.en: It put differently.
sentences.zh: 换个说法。

sentences.en: One of the things that he was doing was he was just training himself to pay attention to the non-linguistic clues that we give each other.
sentences.zh: 他当时在做的一件事，其实就是训练自己去关注我们彼此释放的非语言线索。

sentences.en: And sometimes it's just as simple as that, just reminding ourselves, like, pay attention to where the person's eyes are,
sentences.zh: 有时事情就是这么简单，只需提醒自己，比如，注意看对方的眼睛在哪里，

sentences.en: pay attention to whether they seem to be laughing with me or not.
sentences.zh: 注意看他们似乎在和自己一起笑，还是没有。

sentences.en: These are just little things, little ways to remind ourselves, much like looping for understanding, right?
sentences.zh: 这些都只是小事情，是提醒我们的小方法，就像为了理解而进行的回环确认一样，对吧？

sentences.en: They're just little mnemonics almost to remind us what we already know about communication.
sentences.zh: 它们几乎就像是小助记符，提醒我们那些关于沟通的已知常识。

sentences.en: And it can feel overwhelming, but it doesn't have to be that they're all little things that if we just become more,
sentences.zh: 这可能会让人觉得有点应接不暇，但其实大可不必，这些都是一些小事情，只要我们让它们变得更

sentences.en: more habitualized around doing them, suddenly we start having much better conversations.
sentences.zh: 更加习惯化，不知不觉中，我们的对话就会变得好得多。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Charles, that's such a fascinating story.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯，这个故事太迷人了。

sentences.en: Um, and it hits on, I think another really foundational principle of social interaction, which is mimicry, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且它触及了我认为社交互动的另一个非常基础的原则，那就是模仿，对吧？

sentences.en: A really good predictor of how someone's going to behave is how they're being treated, right?
sentences.zh: 一个人将如何表现，一个很好的预测指标就是别人是如何对待他的，对吧？

sentences.en: We're just hopelessly entrained to one another's behavior, right?
sentences.zh: 我们只是无可救药地与彼此的行为同频共振，对吧？

sentences.en: And you see mimicry in so many different dimensions of human interaction, right?
sentences.zh: 你会在人类互动的许多不同维度中看到模仿的影子，对吧？

sentences.en: We, one person looks at something, we look at the same thing, right?
sentences.zh: 比如一个人看向某样东西，我们也会看向同一样东西，对吧？

sentences.en: We mimic each other in body posture.
sentences.zh: 我们在身体姿势上模仿彼此。

sentences.en: We mimic each other in gestures and facial expressions and emotion and tone of voice.
sentences.zh: 我们在手势、面部表情、情绪和语调上都在模仿彼此。

sentences.en: And certainly in the words we use too.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们在使用的词汇上也是如此。

sentences.en: Um, and that can be a really powerful tool, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这可以成为一个非常强大的工具，对吧？

sentences.en: If we, that is unconscious cues and mimicry that signal that someone is on the same wavelength as us, that there's a bit of a shared reality, right?
sentences.zh: 如果我们……这些无意识的线索和模仿表明某人和我们处于同一频段，表明我们之间存在某种共享的现实，对吧？

sentences.en: That we're enjoying the same things about the situation or, or, you know, miserating about the same things about the situation, right?
sentences.zh: 表明我们对当前局势有着相同的乐趣，或者，你知道的，在为局势中的某些不如意而共同抱怨，对吧？

sentences.en: That we're seeing things in the same way.
sentences.zh: 表明我们以同样的方式看待事物。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: But I think this is a powerful tool.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这是一个强大的工具。

sentences.en: You know, I think in our work on disagreement, we're focusing a lot on the role of mimicry.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我认为我们在研究分歧时，把很大一部分精力放在了模仿的作用上。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, we're always, we're very often focused on how we can get other people to treat us with more respect, right?
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道的，我们总是、非常经常地关注如何能让别人以更多的尊重来对待我们，对吧？

sentences.en: How we can encourage others to demonstrate receptiveness to us.
sentences.zh: 我们如何才能鼓励他人向我们表现出接受度。

sentences.en: And we found that one of the most powerful ways to encourage receptiveness in others is to be receptive yourself, right?
sentences.zh: 我们发现，鼓励他人接受度最强大的方法之一，就是让自己本身变得具有接受度，对吧？

sentences.en: That it improves other people's view of us and also all of our counterparts.
sentences.zh: 这能改善别人对我们的看法，也能改善我们所有对话伙伴的看法。

sentences.en: And we can actually create these micro cultures of respect and trust simply by making that choice ourself.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上只需自己做出这种选择，就能创造出这些充满尊重和信任的微文化。

sentences.en: It's not sort of a one-to-one relationship, but the more we can express it ourselves, the more
sentences.zh: 这并不是某种一一对应的关系，但我们自己表达得越多，

sentences.en: that people sort of unconsciously pick up on that, that, that tone and, and, and will reflect it back to us.
sentences.zh: 人们就越会无意识地捕捉到那种语气，并且会将其反射给我们。

sentences.en: And so even if it feels a little unnatural at first, it wants that cycle of respect starts
sentences.zh: 因此，即使一开始感觉有点不自然，但一旦那种相互尊重的循环开始

sentences.en: revving up, it starts to feel real and, and, and hopefully, um, can create a little more of a safe space.
sentences.zh: 运转起来，它就会开始变得真实，并且希望、嗯，能够营造出更多一点的安全空间。

sentences.en: Um, you know, that maybe you didn't feel possible when you get started.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，这或许在刚开始时是你觉得不可能实现的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I think that's a really good point.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一个非常好的观点。

sentences.en: And, and it, it kind of raises this thing that we haven't talked about yet, but which of course is underlies all of this, which is the reason why
sentences.zh: 而且，它其实引出了一个我们还没谈过、但它当然是这一切基础的问题，那就是为什么

sentences.en: mimicry is so important and so powerful is because in many ways, mimicry is the point of communication, right?
sentences.zh: 模仿如此重要、如此强大，因为在许多方面，模仿正是交流的意义所在，对吧？

sentences.en: We haven't talked about neural entrainment and the work from Uri Hassan and Talia Wheatley
sentences.zh: 我们还没聊过神经同频（neural entrainment）以及尤里·哈桑（Uri Hassan）和塔利亚·韦特利（Talia Wheatley）的研究，

sentences.en: looking at how our, our bodies become similar when we're in a, when we're in conversation with each other, our eyes sometimes start dilating at the same rate.
sentences.zh: 他们的研究发现，当我们彼此交谈时，我们的身体会变得相似，我们的瞳孔有时会以相同的频率放大。

sentences.en: We start breathing in similar ways, but most importantly, our brains become more similar.
sentences.zh: 我们开始以类似的方式呼吸，但最重要的是，我们的大脑变得越来越相似。

sentences.en: And, and that's kind of the goal of communication, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是交流的目的，对吧？

sentences.en: Is, is if I'm feeling a certain emotion and I threw my words can inspire you to feel that same emotion, then we have some level of understanding where we're communing with
sentences.zh: 那就是，如果我感受到了某种情绪，并且我通过我的言语能够激发你也去感受那种情绪，那么我们就达到了一定程度的理解，我们在彼此

sentences.en: each other.
sentences.zh: 共鸣。

sentences.en: And this mimicry is part of communication.
sentences.zh: 而这种模仿正是交流的一部分。

sentences.en: It's in some ways, the point of communication is for us to align our thoughts and our emotions and our beliefs, at least enough to understand what
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，交流的意义就在于让我们调整彼此的思想、情绪和信念，至少调整到能够理解彼此

sentences.en: each other is saying and to transmit an idea or a feeling.
sentences.zh: 所言，并传递一个想法或一种感受的程度。

sentences.en: And I think that's really, really powerful.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这真的、真的很强大。

sentences.en: And if, if we're focused on that as a goal, then mimicry doesn't become sort of this slavish devotion to someone else's, to imitating someone else.
sentences.zh: 而且，如果我们把这作为目标，那么模仿就不会变成某种对别人的盲目顺从、对别人的盲目模仿。

sentences.en: It rather becomes the path to actually achieving communion.
sentences.zh: 相反，它成了真正实现心灵相通的途径。

sentences.en: So I want to ask one question to wrap up here and I'll ask you both.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想在这里问最后一个问题，我要问你们两个。

sentences.en: Has your work in this area changed the way that you talk with people and what lessons have you put into practice in your own life?
sentences.zh: 你们在这一领域的工作是否改变了你们与人交谈的方式？你们在自己的生活中付诸实践了哪些经验？

sentences.en: And for you, Charles, did you become a better manager?
sentences.zh: 对你而言，查尔斯，你有没有成为一个更好的管理者？

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And actually, I mean, I will say it has revolutionized how I communicate.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我的意思是，我要说它彻底革新了我的沟通方式。

sentences.en: I mean, not just, not just with people at work, but also, you know, with my wife, with my kids.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不仅是在工作中与人沟通，还包括，你知道的，与我的妻子、与我的孩子。

sentences.en: I mean, it's, it's just taught me to think so much more deeply about how I'm communicating and that can sound like a burden, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它教会我去更深刻地思考我是如何沟通的，这听起来可能像个负担，对吧？

sentences.en: Like it makes every conversation kind of this mental struggle.
sentences.zh: 就像让每一次谈话都变成了一种心理挣扎。

sentences.en: But actually what I found is that, is that it makes communication much easier.
sentences.zh: 但实际上我发现，它让沟通变得容易得多了。

sentences.en: Like I actually get to think less because, because I know that I should ask a follow-up question or I know that I should,
sentences.zh: 就像我实际上不需要想那么多了，因为我知道我应该问一个后续问题，或者我知道我应该

sentences.en: I should reciprocate vulnerability when someone is vulnerable with me.
sentences.zh: 在别人向我展现脆弱时报以同样的脆弱。

sentences.en: You know, one of the first things that like often happens when I'm talking to my wife and there's a shorthand we use for this
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我和妻子谈话时经常发生的一件事是，我们为此使用了一种简写方式，

sentences.en: with that, that I think has become popular in schools, which is when we start talking to each other, we say, so do you want me to hear you?
sentences.zh: 我认为这种方式在学校里已经流行开来，那就是当我们开始交谈时，我们会说：“所以，你是希望我倾听你？

sentences.en: Do you want me to help you?
sentences.zh: 你是希望我帮你想办法？

sentences.en: Or do you want me to hug you?
sentences.zh: 还是希望我给你一个拥抱？”

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: And this is, this is basically back to the beginning of our conversation.
sentences.zh: 这其实回到了我们对话的开端。

sentences.en: This is asking them what their goal is.
sentences.zh: 这就是在询问他们的目标是什么。

sentences.en: Like, do you want me to solve it?
sentences.zh: 就像，“你是想让我解决它吗？

sentences.en: Is this a practical conversation?
sentences.zh: 这是一场务实的对话吗？

sentences.en: You want me to help you solve it?
sentences.zh: 你想要我帮你解决它吗？

sentences.en: Or do you want me just to, to hear your emotions, which is, you know, the, uh, an emotional listening conversation or, or do you want me to, to hug you to sort of a social
sentences.zh: 还是你只是想让我倾听你的情绪？”也就是，你知道的，进行情感倾听的对话，或者你想让我给你

sentences.en: conversation to show you that we are still together and simply asking that question has like, and I ask
sentences.zh: 一个拥抱，这是一种社交对话，向你表明我们仍然在一起。仅仅提出这个问题，就像……我

sentences.en: it all the time now I drive people crazy with it, but like, but like it, it's this magical thing that all of a sudden people say like, Oh, I want you to hear me.
sentences.zh: 现在总是问这个问题，我把周围人都快逼疯了，但它就是有这样一种神奇的效果，大家突然就会说：“哦，我想让你倾听我。”

sentences.en: And then I know what my job is and they know what their job is and things go so much more smoothly.
sentences.zh: 然后我就知道我的工作是什么了，他们也知道他们的工作是什么，事情就会顺利得多。

sentences.en: Mike, what about you?
sentences.zh: 迈克，你呢？

sentences.en: That's a really good one.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常棒的例子。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it's so funny with science.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得科学真的很有趣。

sentences.en: I do, I do think we're making a lot of progress, but sometimes the more you study a subject, the less you feel like you know about it.
sentences.zh: 我的确觉得我们在取得很大进展，但有时你对一个课题研究得越多，你就越觉得自己对它一无所知。

sentences.en: And, and for me, you know, I, I do a lot of follow-up questions.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，你知道的，我做了很多后续提问。

sentences.en: I do a lot of, uh, conversational receptiveness.
sentences.zh: 我做了很多关于对话接受度的事情。

sentences.en: I think, I think my disagreements are more productive, although you'd have to ask my, my colleagues at Imperial college about that.
sentences.zh: 我认为，我的分歧处理得更有建设性了，尽管你得去问问我在帝国理工学院的同事们是不是这样。

sentences.en: Um, you know, I, I, it's, it's more the deep humility, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，这更多的是一种深沉的谦逊，对吧？

sentences.en: I plan to be surprised and, and I, and I plan to learn from people because it's just so much more complicated than you can anticipate going forward.
sentences.zh: 我时刻准备着感到惊讶，我准备着向人们学习，因为事情远比你在着手去做之前预料的要复杂得多。

sentences.en: I always feel like there's so much more to learn than I could ever get out of one conversation.
sentences.zh: 我总觉得有太多东西要学，远超我从单次对话中能汲取的全部。

sentences.en: I've learned a lot with, with the two of you today, more than planned even.
sentences.zh: 今天跟你们俩在一起，我学到了很多，甚至超出了原计划。

sentences.en: Yeah, me too.
sentences.zh: 是的，我也是。

sentences.en: Well, I want to thank you both for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 好的，我要感谢你们两位今天能来参加节目。

sentences.en: I think it was a great conversation.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一次非常棒的对话。

sentences.en: Me too.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 不用谢。

sentences.en: It's been a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 非常荣幸。
